purpose: Close the one genuine Source Gap in B5: expected compensation and mixed acid-base disorder detection. Existing project Lectures remain Primary for water/Na/K/Ca, renal acid handling and 306 source-specific treatment Precision.

sources.title: Acid-Base Disorders
allowed_claims: ABG/serum-electrolyte acid-base evaluation using pH, PaCO2 and HCO3-.
Mixed disorder suspicion when measured PaCO2/HCO3- does not match expected compensation.
Anion gap calculation in metabolic acidosis and delta-gap use for detecting an additional metabolic process.
Winter formula for expected respiratory compensation in metabolic acidosis.
Interpretation of measured PaCO2 above/below Winter expected range as additional respiratory acidosis/alkalosis.

sources.title: Primary Changes and Compensations in Simple Acid-Base Disorders
allowed_claims: Metabolic acidosis expected PaCO2: 1.5 x HCO3- + 8 +/- 2 mmHg (Winter formula).
Metabolic alkalosis expected PaCO2: rise about 0.6-0.75 mmHg per 1 mmol/L HCO3- rise, with compensatory PaCO2 generally not above about 55 mmHg.
Respiratory acidosis: acute HCO3- rise about 1-2 mmol/L per 10 mmHg PaCO2 rise; chronic rise about 3-4 mmol/L per 10 mmHg.
Respiratory alkalosis: acute HCO3- fall about 1-2 mmol/L per 10 mmHg PaCO2 fall; chronic fall about 4-5 mmol/L per 10 mmHg.

allowed_algorithm: 1. Assess pH/acidemia/alkalemia while remembering a mixed disorder may yield near-normal pH.
2. Identify the dominant metabolic (HCO3-) or respiratory (PaCO2) direction from pH/PaCO2/HCO3- and clinical context.
3. Calculate expected compensation for the proposed primary disorder.
4. If measured compensation falls outside the expected range, diagnose/suspect an additional primary acid-base process rather than calling it 'over/under compensation'.
5. In metabolic acidosis, calculate AG = Na - (Cl + HCO3-); elevated AG indicates a high-anion-gap metabolic-acidosis component.

6. In metabolic acidosis, use delta gap = measured AG - chosen normal AG; add delta gap to measured HCO3-. A corrected HCO3- above the normal range supports additional metabolic alkalosis. A normal-gap low-HCO3-/high-Cl pattern supports non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis.
7. Reconcile the acid-base calculation with the actual disease context before final diagnosis.
